items.title: Delhi court seeks police reply to Congress MP and JNU professor A Bimol Akoijam's anticipatory bail plea
items.summary: A Delhi court on Tuesday sought a response from Delhi Police reply on an anticipatory bail plea filed by Congress Member of Parliament (MP) and Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) professor A Bimol Akoijam in connection with the sexual harassment case against him. Several students have levelled allegations of sexual harassment against Akoijam, pursuant to which the Delhi Police registered a first information report (FIR) for offences of sexual harassment under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Special Judge Digvinay Singh of the Rouse Avenue Courts heard Akoijam's anticipatory bail plea today and sought the police's reply. Judge Singh said that no action will be taken against A Bimol Akoijam till November 5, when the matter will be heard next. The Court also said the investigating officer must appear in Court on the next date of hearing. Akoijam's counsel told the Court today that he received transit anticipatory bail from a court in Manipur, which the Patiala House Court extended on October 29. items.title: Can't let women, children fall prey to buses and die: Kerala High Court calls for strict measures
items.summary: The Kerala High Court Tuesday expressed serious concern over reckless driving by bus drivers and speeding cars and the rising number of road accidents in the State, calling for concrete measures to prevent further loss of lives [ Suo Motu v The Chief Secretary and ors and connected cases ]. A bench of Justice Raja Vijayaraghavan V and Justice KV Jayakumar suggested permanent cancellation of driving license or impounding offending vehicles to curb road mishaps. "If it is done repeatedly, your licence will go, or vehicle. Some action will have to be taken. Everything is being taken lightly and the corrective measures are not being taken," the Court remarked. The Court was hearing a suo motu petition concerning road safety in Kerala. "We can't just permit all the children, women to fall prey to the buses and go underneath the tyres and die. Why would we want to do that? Come up with something," the Court said. Justice Vijayaraghavan questioned the authorities over their failure to effectively implement existing road safety guidelines. items.summary: The Allahabad High Court has directed the police to register a criminal case against a woman for allegedly getting a false rape case registered against her brother by using her own daughter. Justice Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal took note of the victim's statement before the trial court that her uncle had merely scolded her for use of a mobile phone. "From a perusal of the statements of P.W.-1 and P.W.-2, it is clear that P.W.-2 (first informant) has lodged a false case against the applicant, and this fact has been admitted by her in her statement before the trial court. Therefore, the Senior Superintendent of Police, Meerut, is directed to register an F.I.R. against P.W.-2 (first informant) for lodging a false case against the applicant, as per Section 22 of the POCSO Act," the Court directed. The Court passed the order on October 28 while granting bail to the accused who has been booked by Meerut police under various provisions of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act. items.title: Supreme Court deletes High Court strictures against POCSO judge over ‘cut, copy and paste’ judgment
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently expunged adverse remarks and strictures passed by the Rajasthan High Court against a woman judicial officer who was accused of using a "cut, copy and paste" approach while writing a judgment in a Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act case [ In Re: XXX, a Judicial Officer in The District Judge Cadre of Rajasthan Judicial Services ]. A Bench of Justices Sandeep Mehta and Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya set aside the High Court's directions ordering the entry of the remarks into the judge's annual confidential report (ACR) and sending her for judgment-writing training. items.title: Qadeemi Masjid is incompatible with secular character of Krishi Bhawan, will be demolished: Centre to Delhi HC
items.summary: The Central government has informed the Delhi High Court that the century-old mosque in Krishi Bhawan will be removed because retaining a religious structure in an office complex is “impermissible and incompatible with the secular character" of government property. In an affidavit filed in the Court, the government said that Krishi Bhawan and the Central Secretariat complex are secular premises dedicated exclusively to governmental, administrative and public service functions. "The establishment or retention of a permanent religious structure, or a demand for one, within the confines of a central government office complex is impermissible and incompatible with the secular character of Government property. That the public land situated within a central administrative zone cannot be encumbered by any permanent religious reservation," the government said. It added that there is a mosque located at India Gate in the two kilometre radius. "[It] is fully functional to serve as a proximate prayer facility for any individuals seeking one nearby," the government said. items.title: Madhya Pradesh High Court quashes FIR against journalist over report on Ganesh Visarjan procession violence
items.summary: The Madhya Pradesh High Court recently quashed a criminal case against a journalist accused of promoting enmity through a news report on an incident of violence during a Ganesh Visarjan procession in 2025 [Uvesh Khan @ Uvesh Reporter vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh] Justice Himanshu Joshi said that mere reporting of an incident involving violence does not constitute the offence of promoting enmity or disharmony between different groups under Section 196(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). "The nature and content of the publication, the context in which it was made, and the requisite connection with the promotion or attempted promotion of enmity between groups are material considerations," the Court said. It added that the freedom of speech and expression guaranteed under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution cannot be curtailed merely because a report concerns a sensitive public incident. Any restriction on such expression must be justified in law, the bench said. items.title: Account blocking by LinkedIn to be challenged through civil suit, not writ petition: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that a writ petition is not maintainable against LinkedIn or its resident grievance officer over their decision to block/restrict an account [Mayank Jain v. Union of India & Ors] . Justice Amit Mahajan held that the threshold for a private entity to be amenable to writ jurisdiction is that it must undertake functions that are fundamentally governmental in nature or are performed by virtue of power vested by law. The Court underscored that LinkedIn does not perform a public function or public duty. “While the platform provided by Respondent No. 2 [LinkedIn] plays a significant role in disseminating information and shaping public opinion, its primary function is to provide a platform for expression, with public discourse being a consequence of its operations rather than a public duty. Its operations remain private in nature, and no governmental mandate delegates any traditional State function to it. Respondent No. 2 is neither obligated to provide such a platform in discharge of a public duty nor legally compelled to offer its services, which are voluntary and user-driven,” the Court observed.
